9368.explanation: The question, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?" was asked following the call of Matthew (Levi) to be a disciple of Jesus. This event is recorded in Matthew 9:9-13, Mark 2:13-17, and Luke 5:27-32. After Jesus called Matthew to follow Him, Matthew hosted a great feast in his house, and tax collectors and sinners were present. 9410.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
9410.question_text: ''If your enemy is hungry, feed him.'' This statement implies
9410.explanation:
The statement "If your enemy is hungry, feed him" is based on the principle of showing kindness and compassion, even to those who may oppose or harm you. It reflects a spirit of mercy and care, as seen in Romans 12:20 (RSV), which says:

"If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by so doing you will heap burning coals upon his head."

This statement encourages responding to an enemy with kindness, rather than with hostility or vengeance. It is about overcoming evil with good.
